mechanisms.name: compaction-engine-seam
mechanisms.what: `ctx.compaction` is an abstract `CompactionEngine` service with three entry points: `compactIfNeeded(agent, trigger, signal)` for automatic policy (`pressure` or `context-overflow`), `compactNow(agent, signal, sourceCommandId)` for an explicit idle-session compaction, and `compactRegion(start, end, agent, signal)` for a caller-chosen inclusive surface span. Implementations own trigger policy, retention and summarization; the seam fixes the contract that a successful run replaces the selected surface span with one summary node and prevents concurrent compaction of the same session. Exactly one implementation is loaded per context.
invariants: the replacement user message must use `compactCheckpointSource` with the transaction's CompactionId so consumers can recognise it independently of the backend
compactRegion edges name surface POSITIONS, not numeric seq order, and must be tool-pairing balanced
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed - the abstract seam declares `ManualCompactionError` codes busy/cancelled/changed/summary/commit/persistence for the manual path and an exact abort reason for cancellation; a failed attempt stays visible in the log
constants: ManualCompactionErrorCode: busy, cancelled, changed, summary, commit, persistence

mechanisms.name: compaction-durable-bracket-transaction
mechanisms.what: One compaction run is a durable transaction bracketed by two log markers. `compaction/start` (carrying compactionId, optional sourceCommandId and the owning turn) is appended BEFORE summarization yields and acts as the lock; an unmatched start makes any other compaction attempt fail busy, unless a later constructor-seed boundary proves the marker belongs to an earlier session lifecycle. After summarization the selected span is re-asserted stable, then `compaction/summary` and the replacement `user/message` are appended together without yielding, and `compaction/end` closes the bracket. A closure failure deliberately leaves the unmatched start detectable; on error the end marker records the errorChain.
invariants: the durable start marker is the lock - never a process-local flag
a summary may only be committed if the selected span is still the same present, contiguous, equally priced, balanced replacement target
`compaction/end` is attempted on every exit path, including failure
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed - the unmatched `compaction/start` marker makes subsequent compaction attempts fail busy rather than run concurrently; failed attempts remain durable in the log

mechanisms.name: surface-replace-projection
mechanisms.what: The model-visible surface is a projection over the append-only log, not a rewrite of it. `SurfaceManager` folds surface-eligible events (system/message, user/message, assistant/message, tool/result) into an ordered node list, applying `surfaceOp: 'append'` at the tail or `surfaceOp: {op:'replace', startSeq, endSeq}` as a positional substitution, and tracks a monotonic `replaceGeneration`. Compaction lands as a replace whose `sourceEventSeqs` must cite every shadowed node; append-origin events remain the durable human transcript.
invariants: `sourceEventSeqs` must densely cite earlier events, contain no duplicates, and include every shadowed surface node
a replacement covering surface node 0 while it holds the system prompt must itself be a system/message over exactly that node
a tool/result replacement must rewrite exactly one current tool/result and may change only content
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed - every rule is an assertion in `planSurfaceEvent`; a violation throws and the fold refuses the event instead of producing a divergent surface

mechanisms.name: pressure-threshold-compaction-policy
mechanisms.what: `compaction-basic` decides automatic compaction from the routed model's own capacity: it reads the latest durable `request/header` config, resolves that exact provider/model's context window through `ctx.llm.resolveModelInfo`, scales the policy into `thresholdTokens = floor(contextWindow * thresholdRatio)` and `retainTokens = floor(contextWindow * retainRatio)`, and compacts only when the measured total reaches the threshold. It lands the model-free prune pass first, remeasures, then loops up to `compactionRetries` summary attempts; per-model overrides can replace every policy field for one exact route.
invariants: retainTokens must be strictly less than thresholdTokens
retainRatio must be strictly less than thresholdRatio
policy for a route with no declared contextWindow raises TargetPressureConfigError instead of guessing
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed - a step-pressure failure is logged as a warning and the turn continues; a missing context capacity is reported once per target and suppressed afterwards; exhausting all retries still above threshold throws

mechanisms.name: context-overflow-recovery
mechanisms.what: When a model attempt fails with the provider-confirmed context-window-exceeded code, `compaction-basic` intercepts the `agent/request-error` waterfall, forces a compaction bypassing the normal threshold and retained-tail policy (`selectCompactableRange(..., 0)`), and returns `{kind:'retry'}` so the loop retries the step from the replacement surface. The retry budget is per agent and is reset on idle and on any successful `assistant/message`, so tool-call continuations start a fresh overflow sequence.
invariants: overflow compaction ignores the pressure threshold and retention floor
a durable surface generation advance is required before a retry is requested
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft - a recovery failure that nonetheless produced durable surface progress still counts as retry proof and increments the budget; a recovery failure with no durable progress logs a warning and preserves the original request error; cancellation always prevents the retry

mechanisms.name: tool-result-pruner
mechanisms.what: A model-free, replay-safe pruner service (`ctx.toolResultPruner`) that rewrites over-budget tool results in place on the current surface. It measures text content in Unicode code points (non-text blocks cost zero), and for any result above `thresholdChars` keeps a head and a tail around a fixed marker, splitting by code point so a surrogate pair is never broken. Each rewrite appends a `compaction/prune` shadow-price event immediately before the replacement `tool/result` carrying a single-node replace surfaceOp citing the shadowed seq.
invariants: headChars + marker + tailChars must be at most thresholdChars
the emitted replacement must be strictly smaller than the original and within threshold
each metering event and its replacement are appended synchronously adjacent
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed - a replacement that would not shrink or that exceeds the threshold throws; replacements committed earlier in the same pass remain durable

mechanisms.name: replay-aware-token-meter
mechanisms.what: `ctx.tokenMeter` is the single measurement service: it replays each session's durable tail into a per-session fold (surface nodes with prices, the latest request header, the open step, and a measurement anchor) and reports baseline, surface delta and total tokens. Provider usage is reused only when the anchored call's canonical request envelope equals the current header and its total is no lower than the fully repriced anchor; otherwise the whole envelope and surface are repriced. It also registers the `tokenUsage`, `contextPressure` and `contextBreakdown` session projections so clients read the same numbers.
invariants: every fallible step of the fold (surface plan, anchor validation) runs before any state mutation, so a malformed event stays unread on retry instead of half-applying
measurement is O(surface) and clones its positional nodes
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed - a `step/start` without a matching end, an unmatched `step/end`, or an `assistant/message` with no matching `step/start` throws during the fold
constants: no settings are supported (TokenMeterConfig rejects every key)

mechanisms.name: system-prompt-assembly
mechanisms.what: `ctx.systemPrompt` assembles the model input from named, scoped contributions: sections (ordered text), contexts (dynamic runtime-context fragments), variable providers, and tool-schema providers. Section positions come from a central `SECTION_ORDERS` table so first-party sections cannot collide, tools are canonically ordered by a configured `toolOrder` with a mandatory `<unlisted-tools>` rest marker (default lexicographic), and `{{variable}}` references are strict - a malformed, unknown or undefined reference throws and substituted text is not rescanned. Later layers (agent scope) shadow earlier ones by name.
invariants: toolOrder must contain the `<unlisted-tools>` rest entry exactly once and may not name an unregistered tool
`{{variable}}` references are strict and never resolved through Object.prototype
a scoped registration shadows the global one with the same name instead of duplicating it
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed - registration conflicts, unknown order entries and bad variable references all throw, at load time where possible and at assembly time otherwise
constants: SECTION_ORDERS span -1000 (harness identity) to 10200 (deployment persona suffix)

mechanisms.name: runtime-context-snapshot-projection
mechanisms.what: Dynamic per-step context (sandbox policy, approval policy, delegation policy, time, tmux, ...) is committed as an append-origin `user/message` whose text is a single snapshot that explicitly supersedes earlier snapshots. `RuntimeContextProjection` restores the last retained snapshot by scanning the durable log newest-first against the current surface, follows `session/event` afterwards, and only emits a new snapshot when the rendered value differs; when every contributor goes away it emits a fixed cleared marker instead of deleting history.
invariants: a snapshot is only emitted when its rendered value differs from the retained one
the cleared marker carries no contributing sections to attribute
restoration is durable, not process-local - a resumed process reconstructs the retained snapshot from the log
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft - absence of any contributor means no snapshot is emitted and the cleared marker (if any) is only written once
constants: CLEARED = 'Current runtime context: none. Earlier runtime-context snapshots no longer apply.'

mechanisms.name: prompt-series-and-surface-generation-tracking
mechanisms.what: The loop keeps provider prompt-cache continuity explicit. `SystemPromptProjection` decides per step whether the rendered prompt is appended as a new `system/message` after the cached history (a capable route in an unbroken series) or normalises surface node 0 and empties later active system nodes (an incapable route, a broken series, or a cleared prompt), using `replace` intents. The decision inputs are the route's in-history capability, whether the step starts a series, and whether the prompt text changed; dormant empty tails do not force repeated replacements.
invariants: the first prompt, even empty, reserves surface node 0
empty tails are inert: they supply no effective text and need no repeated replacement
a series restart is triggered by a pre-step declaration, a surface replacement generation change, or an assembled-tool change
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft - an unchanged prompt produces no commit at all, so no unnecessary surface churn

mechanisms.name: agent-instructions-discovery
mechanisms.what: A workspace instruction loader that discovers and injects AGENTS.md-compatible files. It resolves the project root from configured markers, walks the ancestor chain plus descendant directories between the root and any touched path, loads user-global instructions from `$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md`, dedups by directory, hashes content into an instruction digest, and renders the result as a `<system-reminder>` envelope with the closing tag escaped. Touches of read/write/edit file paths trigger re-projection of the relevant scope instructions.
invariants: instruction content is identified by a digest so unchanged files do not re-inject
the closing `</system-reminder>` sequence in instruction text is escaped
a visible baseline is replaced only when its identity changes
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft - a disabled byte budget or a missing filesystem service yields no projection; projection composes are serialized per agent

mechanisms.name: file-reference-seam
mechanisms.what: `ctx.fileReferences` is an abstract host capability for cancellable `@`-path discovery: a UI submits the path text following `@` or `@"` and receives deterministic path-only candidates bounded by the agent's session cwd. The plugin also exports the exact model-facing `FILE_REFERENCE_PROMPT` guidance and the `@`-token grammar (`activeAtToken`, `formatFileMention`) so renderer and engine agree on the syntax. There is no production caller inside the host core - the consumer is the browser client's input surface.
invariants: discovery is bounded by the agent's session cwd
candidates are path-only; the model is told not to claim it inspected a file before reading it
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft - cancellable async discovery; the seam declares no retry or caching

mechanisms.name: tmux-location-context-injection
mechanisms.what: An opt-in pre-step listener pulls the agent process's tmux location once per turn (step 1) through the `ctx.shell` executor and injects it as durable, source-attributed context naming session, window, pane and the window layout. Genuineness is verified by matching the pane's `#{pane_tty}` against this process's own controlling terminal, so a terminal that merely inherited `$TMUX`/`$TMUX_PANE` from an ancestor reads as "not in tmux". Re-injection only happens when the rendered state changed, with an optional floor between injections.
invariants: the durable injection is compared on its stable state block, excluding the volatile turn preamble
the schedule is reconstructed from the durable log, so it survives compaction and process restarts
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-open - absent tmux environment, an inherited-only environment, an absent `ctx.shell`, or a failed query is a no-op, and an executor rejection is logged as a warning and the turn continues
constants: TMUX_FIELDS = 8 tab-separated format fields including window_layout
refreshIntervalMs: optional non-negative safe integer, 0/omitted means inject on every eligible change

mechanisms.name: time-context-injection
mechanisms.what: A pre-step listener injects a timestamp reading (turn, step, formatted time, optional browser time zone, and elapsed time since the preceding model-visible message or step context) as durable plugin-sourced context. A `timeContext` session projection (stateVersion 2) tracks last message time, last injection time and last turn injection time so re-injection is rate-limited and turn boundaries reset the per-turn gate.
invariants: an invalid or unresolvable time zone throws at plugin apply, not at request time
refreshIntervalMs must be a non-negative safe integer
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed at load (bad time zone or interval throws), fail-soft at request time (re-injection suppressed while within the interval)

mechanisms.name: context-window-resolution
mechanisms.what: Context capacity is adapter-owned model metadata, not a harness constant. `ctx.llm.resolveModelInfo(provider, model)` normalises the adapter's resolved model info and rejects a non-positive or non-integer `contextWindow`; the loop copies the resolved window into the durable `request/context` event, and compaction-basic reads it back to scale its pressure threshold. Model info carries context and max-output metadata alongside the model id.
invariants: a declared contextWindow must be a positive integer
the resolved envelope is persisted on `request/context` so later policy can be re-derived from the log
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed - a malformed adapter context throws during normalisation rather than being clamped
